# Part C label sensitivity (generated by `c5_label_sensitivity.py`)

> **This is a sensitivity analysis, not a re-labelling.** The fresh-set answer key is unchanged. It was made by an LLM (Claude), and the human spot-check is still pending. Each section asks how far a conclusion would move if labels or reference numbers were different.

Labels: `data/fresh/labels.csv`; 349 labelled sentences (negative 27, neutral 210, positive 112). "Ours" = the frozen 3-seed ensemble unless a seed is named.

## a) FinMA's lead on the fresh set alone

FinMA − ours, weighted F1: **-0.0209**, 95% CI **[-0.057, +0.016]**. The CI includes 0: on fresh data alone, neither system is ahead.

*Paired bootstrap: each of 2000 replicates resamples the 349 fresh sentences with replacement and scores both systems on the same draw; percentile interval; numpy `default_rng(0)` drawing fresh indices only. Drawing them as the fresh half of c4_report.py's two-set stream instead gives [-0.058, +0.014]: the endpoints carry about ±0.002 of Monte Carlo noise.*

## b) Each system vs FinMA-7B on the fresh set (McNemar)

| System | Fresh wF1 | wF1 − FinMA | Only this right / only FinMA right | McNemar p (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E4B-it zero-shot | 0.7164 | -0.0741 | 20 / 46 | 0.0019 |
| Ours, seed 3407 | 0.8237 | +0.0332 | 32 / 19 | 0.092 |
| Ours, seed 42 | 0.8089 | +0.0184 | 27 / 20 | 0.38 |
| Ours, seed 7 | 0.7969 | +0.0065 | 27 / 24 | 0.78 |
| Ours, 3-seed ensemble | 0.8114 | +0.0209 | 27 / 19 | 0.3 |

*None of our models differ significantly from FinMA on the fresh set (smallest p = 0.092). Our seeds span 0.027 wF1 among themselves, about the size of the FinMA gap.*

## c) Tipping point: label changes needed to flip the Part C verdict

Candidates: the **22** fresh sentences labelled *neutral* that FinMA calls *positive* and our ensemble calls *neutral*. Relabelling one of them *positive* moves one sentence from "only ours right" to "only FinMA right", the change most favourable to FinMA a single label edit can make. - The shrink falls below the 0.03 rule at **k = 7**.
- The CI first includes 0 at **k = 5** in id order; over 50 random orders, at k = 4–5.
- Which sentences are relabelled doesn't change the point estimates: all candidates share the same gold, FinMA and ensemble labels, so any k of them give the same confusion matrices. Only the bootstrap CI depends on the choice, through which sentences each replicate happens to draw.

*k = 0 reproduces c4_report.py exactly (same bootstrap stream). 22 candidates out of 210 neutral-labelled sentences; a human disagreeing with the AI on 7 of them, all in FinMA's favour, would make the result inconclusive.*

## d) FinMA's drop measured from its published score

Part C measures FinMA's drop from our re-run (FinBen test 0.937). FinMA's own paper reports 0.88. Measured from that, the drop is much smaller:

| System | FinBen FPB reference | Fresh wF1 | Drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| FinMA-7B, from our re-run | 0.9371 | 0.7905 | -0.1466 |
| FinMA-7B, from the published score | 0.88 | 0.7905 | **-0.0895** |
| Ours, 3-seed ensemble | 0.8900 | 0.8114 | **-0.0786** |
| E4B-it zero-shot | 0.7944 | 0.7164 | -0.0781 |

With the published number as FinMA's FinBen score, FinMA's FinBen lead is -0.0100 and the shrink is **+0.0109**, 95% CI [-0.030, +0.053] (published score held fixed, everything else resampled as in c4_report.py): by c4_report.py's rule that is **inconclusive** on this reference. The Part C verdict therefore depends on our re-run's 0.937 as FinMA's FinBen score. Our re-run's 0.937 is itself unexplained (5.7 points above the published score; see ANALYSIS.md, Part B).

Rows: gold label (AI-made). Columns: the model's parsed answer.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| total | 24 | 178 | 147 | 0 | 349 |

| gold \ predicted | negative | neutral | positive | missing | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| negative | 17 | 10 | 0 | 0 | 27 |
| neutral | 5 | 138 | 67 | 0 | 210 |
| positive | 0 | 18 | 94 | 0 | 112 |
| total | 22 | 166 | 161 | 0 | 349 |

*Neutral sentences called positive: FinMA 49, ours 31, zero-shot 67. Positive sentences called neutral: FinMA 14, ours 25, zero-shot 18. The neutral/positive border is where the labels matter most: whether a mildly upbeat corporate statement counts as neutral (PhraseBank's convention) or positive decides much of the FinMA gap (section c).*
